enquiry: Our dairy process includes a relatively clear whey stream before a concentration stage. We want to investigate whether spectroscopy can track protein concentration as the stream changes, with laboratory results used as the reference. The stream can become more turbid under some operating conditions. We need a first measurement concept that handles this change rather than assuming the liquid always remains clear.

intake.summary: Customer wants to investigate whether optical spectroscopy can track protein concentration in a dairy whey stream ahead of a concentration stage, using laboratory results as reference, and asks for a first measurement concept that copes with the stream turning more turbid instead of assuming it always stays clear.

recommendations.rationale: Whey is a transparent to semi-transparent dairy liquid, the case for which transmission or transflection is the preferred geometry and gives higher accuracy for low-concentration components. It is the single method to test first, with the optical pathlength controlled for the actual sample.
recommendations.conditions: Applies while the stream stays clear enough for light to cross the measurement path; the pathlength must be set for the real sample and re-checked when the stream changes.

citations.quote: Transmission is the preferred method for transparent or semi-transparent liquids, such as skim milk, whey, or permeate.
transmission is superior for the high-precision analysis of dilute process streams (like whey filtration)
the precise control of the optical pathlength (usually 1 - 10 mm)

recommendations.rationale: NIR reflection is used for opaque or highly concentrated dairy products and works in highly scattering environments, which is what the turbid operating states are. It is kept as a conditional second test because reflection can be less representative for clear liquids.
recommendations.conditions: Applies if the stream becomes too turbid for the transmission path to carry a usable signal.

citations.quote: NIR Reflection is primarily used for opaque or highly concentrated dairy products, such as yogurt, butter, or whole milk concentrates.
reflection can work well in highly scattering environments but can be less representative for clear liquids.
the method is sensitive to the surface characteristics and fat globule size.

recommendations.rationale: MIR gives well-defined absorption bands, including the protein amide bands, and ATR needs only a thin surface layer in contact with the crystal, which can add selectivity that broad NIR bands lack. Combining it with NIR transmission is a later hypothesis, to be tested only if the NIR results fall short of what the process needs.
recommendations.conditions: Applies only if the NIR options cannot reach the accuracy the process needs for protein across the turbidity range.

citations.quote: Mid-IR band spectra contain well-defined peaks (absorption bands), while NIR, UV, and fluorescence spectra contain broad, highly overlapping signals
These are, respectively, the amide I and II bands, two major absorption peaks of the protein peptide group in the infrared region.
The analysis of such systems may require a combination of two or even more spectral methods.

strong absorption in the mid-IR region limits the corresponding spectral method to the analysis of very thin samples (usually less than 50 μm), but it opens up the possibility of using attenuated total reflectance (ATR)
typically at a depth of few microns

measurement_concept.probe_and_geometry: A contact NIR transmission or transflection probe or flow cell at the whey line before the concentration stage; a second NIR reflection window at the same line for the turbid states. A mid-infrared ATR probe is only a later option, and its link length to the spectrometer is an open point.
measurement_concept.location: One measurement point on the whey stream ahead of the concentration stage, chosen where the flow is well mixed and the probe can be cleaned in place.
measurement_concept.fiber_link: Standard Vis-NIR silica fibers are the family for the NIR channels; a mid-infrared channel would need chalcogenide or polycrystalline infrared fibers, for which no achievable process link length is stated in the supplied material.

spectral_ranges.statement: Nominal NIR range 780-2500 nm; the usable range depends on the instrument, fiber and probe actually selected.

citations.quote: NIR spectra (780-2500 nm) contain predominantly overtones and component bands of fundamental vibrations
It is not a product specification: actual spectral coverage, fiber length, component ratings, detection limits and accuracy depend on the configuration and the sample.

spectral_ranges.statement: Nominal MIR range 4000-400 cm-1 (2.5-25 µm); the usable range depends on the crystal, fibers and probe actually selected.

citations.quote: Vibrational spectroscopy in the mid-IR range (4000-400 cm-1) is one of the most informative methods of chemical analysis.
It is not a product specification: actual spectral coverage, fiber length, component ratings, detection limits and accuracy depend on the configuration and the sample.

risks.risk: The stream may become too turbid for a transmission path, so the primary measurement could lose signal exactly in the states the customer wants to cover.

citations.quote: it fails when the milk becomes too "thick" or fat-rich, as the light cannot penetrate the sample.

risks.risk: NIR protein bands are broad and overlap with water, so the calibration is specific to this matrix and must be rebuilt or re-checked when the stream composition changes.

citations.quote: The broad absorption bands observed in this region overlap, suggesting the use of chemometrics for quantitative and qualitative analysis of spectral data.
physical variation; calibration specific to the matrix.

risks.risk: Scatter from fat droplets, protein aggregates or particulates can change the signal independently of protein, so a physical change may look like a concentration change.

citations.quote: the method is sensitive to the surface characteristics and fat globule size.
Morphological factors, such as sample inhomogeneity (e.g., biological tissue) or process turbulence, must also be considered when selecting a measurement technique.

risks.risk: If a second method is added, the ATR crystal and the NIR path sample different depths and volumes and acquire at different rates, so the fused model may not beat the best single method.

citations.quote: It is crucial that the spectral information obtained by different methods-Mid-IR, NIR, Raman, and fluorescence spectra-is collected from the same small, even pinpoint, area of the sample.
data synchronization can be challenging, as the acquisition rates of different spectra can vary greatly-from milliseconds to minutes

steps.step: Collect representative whey samples and process states across the expected range: the clear stream in normal operation and the more turbid states seen under some conditions, at several protein levels, using the same sampling procedure the plant would use.
steps.purpose: Cover the real chemical and physical variation before any model is built.

citations.quote: Representative samples or process states, independent reference measurements, what is compared, and the basis for the go / no-go decision.

steps.step: Measure every sample with the single methods first: NIR transmission or transflection as the primary, and NIR diffuse reflection on the same states, recording turbidity and temperature alongside each spectrum; keep the MIR ATR channel for the later combination test.
steps.purpose: Compare the single methods before any fusion is attempted.

citations.quote: By maintaining both, a lab can calibrate models for every stage of production

steps.step: Take the independent reference: a laboratory protein determination on the same samples, sampled at the same time as the spectra, plus a laboratory turbidity or total-solids value to describe the physical state.
steps.purpose: Give the calibration an independent anchor and record the state the spectra were taken in.

steps.step: Build one calibration per geometry from the reference values and test it on held-out runs or batches, not on random splits of the same run; then compare the single-method models with the later NIR plus MIR ATR fused model.
steps.purpose: Show whether a second method actually adds, rather than only fitting the same data.

steps.step: Agree the go/no-go numbers with the customer before starting (protein range, required accuracy or detection limit, response time, and the turbidity range the concept must survive) and use them to decide whether one geometry, two geometries or an added MIR ATR channel is kept.
steps.purpose: Make the decision rest on the customer's own criteria, not on our judgement of a spectrum.

feasibility_plan.decision_basis: Customer-defined numerical criteria for protein accuracy, detection limit, response time and the turbidity range the concept must survive.

assumptions: The measurement point is a well-mixed section of the whey line ahead of the concentration stage, reachable by a contact probe or flow cell.
The clear state dominates normal operation and the turbid state is an excursion, so a transmission-based primary measurement is worth testing first.
A laboratory protein method exists and can be sampled close enough in time to the spectra to serve as the reference.

solution_options.ease_of_use: Single probe and spectrometer; simplest to operate and calibrate.
solution_options.maintenance: Routine cleaning of one flow cell or probe.
solution_options.performance_fit: Least effort; answers the main question while the stream stays clear.
solution_options.cost_drivers: one spectrometer, one transmission or transflection probe or cell, chemometric calibration and reference analyses

solution_options.ease_of_use: Two geometries, one spectrometer; switching and calibration need care.
solution_options.maintenance: Two probes or windows to clean; the reflection port is prone to fouling.
solution_options.performance_fit: Fits the stated need: covers clear and turbid states with one method.
solution_options.cost_drivers: one spectrometer with two probe geometries, more calibration runs across clear and turbid states, extra reference analyses

solution_options.ease_of_use: Two instruments and fused data; most demanding to run and maintain.
solution_options.maintenance: Per-instrument calibration and drift checks; ATR crystal cleaning.
solution_options.performance_fit: Adds selective protein bands if NIR accuracy falls short across the turbidity range.
solution_options.cost_drivers: a second spectrometer, mid-infrared fiber and ATR probe, data fusion software, per-instrument calibration and maintenance
solution_options.fusion_note: Fusion would start from one model per method and either join the spectral blocks with scaling or combine the per-method results, and only after the single-method tests. The ATR crystal and the NIR path sample different depths and volumes, so the probes must look at the same flowing material and the data must be aligned to a common time step. Each instrument keeps its own calibration, and the fused model must beat the best single method on independent runs before the extra instrument is kept.

assessment.chemometrics_note: Tracking protein quantitatively from NIR needs a calibration model built on laboratory reference values for this stream. Because the bands overlap and the matrix is specific, the model has to be rebuilt or re-checked whenever the stream composition or the turbidity behaviour changes, and it should be tested on held-out runs or batches rather than on random splits of the same run.
assessment.realtime_tracking_note: The measurement is intended in-line and continuous, so the acquisition rate must be fast enough for the process decision and aligned with the timing of the laboratory samples used as reference.
assessment.future_direction: If the trials show that a few informative wavelengths carry the protein signal, a compact spectral fiber sensor for this single measurement point could be a later step, once the laboratory method selection has been made.

proposal.what_would_change_it: If the stream stays clear and NIR transmission meets the agreed protein accuracy, O1 is enough; if the turbidity swings widely or NIR cannot reach the required accuracy, the choice moves to O3 with its mid-infrared ATR channel.
proposal.next_step: Run the feasibility experiment on representative clear and turbid whey samples, starting with NIR transmission, with laboratory protein values as the independent reference.

assessment.brief_answer: Start with NIR transmission (or transflection) on the clear whey stream, using laboratory protein values as the reference; add NIR reflection for the turbid operating states, since transmission loses signal when the liquid becomes thick. Whether NIR alone reaches the protein accuracy you need, and how far the turbidity swings, are still open. Agree the accuracy, range and response time with us before the trials, and we will confirm the geometry and whether a second method is needed.

solution_options.fusion_note: Fusion would start from one model per method and either join the spectral blocks with scaling or combine the per-method results, and only after the single-method tests. The ATR crystal and the NIR path sample different depths and volumes, so the probes must look at the same flowing material and the data must be aligned to a common time step. Each instrument keeps its own calibration, and the fused model must beat the best single method on independent runs before the extra instrument is kept.

assessment_raw.chemometrics_note: Tracking protein quantitatively from NIR needs a calibration model built on laboratory reference values for this stream. Because the bands overlap and the matrix is specific, the model has to be rebuilt or re-checked whenever the stream composition or the turbidity behaviour changes, and it should be tested on held-out runs or batches rather than on random splits of the same run.
assessment_raw.realtime_tracking_note: The measurement is intended in-line and continuous, so the acquisition rate must be fast enough for the process decision and aligned with the timing of the laboratory samples used as reference.
assessment_raw.future_direction: If the trials show that a few informative wavelengths carry the protein signal, a compact spectral fiber sensor for this single measurement point could be a later step, once the laboratory method selection has been made.

proposal.what_would_change_it: If the stream stays clear and NIR transmission meets the agreed protein accuracy, O1 is enough; if the turbidity swings widely or NIR cannot reach the required accuracy, the choice moves to O3 with its mid-infrared ATR channel.
proposal.next_step: Run the feasibility experiment on representative clear and turbid whey samples, starting with NIR transmission, with laboratory protein values as the independent reference.

assessment_raw.brief_answer: Start with NIR transmission (or transflection) on the clear whey stream, using laboratory protein values as the reference; add NIR reflection for the turbid operating states, since transmission loses signal when the liquid becomes thick. Whether NIR alone reaches the protein accuracy you need, and how far the turbidity swings, are still open. Agree the accuracy, range and response time with us before the trials, and we will confirm the geometry and whether a second method is needed.
